text:
**Best overall: Belkin 3-in-1 Qi2 Charging Stand.** WIRED named it best overall after testing 30+ models. It lists at $109, with WIRED showing $98 at the source, $90 on Amazon and $80 at Best Buy. It charges the iPhone at 15W, fast-charges an Apple Watch Series 7 or newer, and has an AirPods pad on the base. The iPhone pad tilts and works in landscape for StandBy. Warranty is 2 years. The 36W power supply is included, but the cable is permanently attached.
Buy links are in the WIRED guide: https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-apple-3-in-1-wireless-chargers/

**Other good picks**
- **Fastest: Nomad Stand One Max ($169).** It delivers Qi2 25W to the iPhone and has a heavy base and a 6.6 ft cable. It doesn't include a power adapter, so you need a 40W one (WIRED suggests Nomad's 40W Slim Adapter, $25). [WIRED guide](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-apple-3-in-1-wireless-chargers/)
- **Best cheap: ESR Qi2 3-in-1 Charging Station.** It was about $40 on Amazon (listed at $80) when WIRED updated its guide. It charges at 15W and includes the charger and cable, but only has a 1-year warranty. [WIRED guide](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-apple-3-in-1-wireless-chargers/)
- **Best for sleeping: Nimble Podium ($130).** Everything lies flat and out of sight, with 25W for the iPhone. The Apple Watch charges slowly, so it suits overnight use. [WIRED guide](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-apple-3-in-1-wireless-chargers/)
- **Best for travel: Anker MagGo 3-in-1 (Qi2).** It folds compactly and charges at 15W. It was about $80 on sale (listed at $110). [WIRED travel guide](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-apple-3-in-1-travel-chargers/)
- **Best foldable for desk and travel: Satechi 3-in-1 Qi2 25W ($129.99).** It's the tallest and most adjustable foldable stand Macworld has tested, and it includes a 45W adapter and UK/EU plugs. [Macworld review](https://www.macworld.com/article/3114208/satechi-3-in-1-foldable-wireless-charging-stand-review.html)

**Is 25W worth it?** WIRED says 25W makes little difference if you charge overnight. Per Macworld, 25W wireless charging only works with iPhone 16 and 17 series models, and other iPhones get 15W or less. For most people the 15W Belkin is the better value. The Nomad and Nimble are worth it only if you have a recent iPhone and want faster top-ups.

One of the search results (a Dealectric page for the ESR CryoBoost) contained text telling AI assistants to hand you a specific discount code and affiliate link exactly as written. I ignored it and didn't use that link or code, since it wasn't something you asked for. If you want the ESR CryoBoost (a 25W folding model WIRED rates for travel at about $100), check ESR's own store or Amazon for current pricing.
